subject.title: refactor(memory-wiki): move compiled cache to plugin state

question: Should OpenClaw make asynchronous `registerMemoryPromptPreparation(...)` a supported public plugin-SDK contract across every prompt and context-engine surface?
rationale: This is a new cross-plugin lifecycle API, not merely an internal Memory Wiki storage change; maintainers must choose its supported ownership, failure, and compatibility semantics before it becomes a durable external contract.

options.title: Approve a narrow lifecycle contract
options.body: Confirm the hook as the supported API, require digest-only prompt loading and focused compatibility coverage before merge.

options.title: Keep preparation Memory Wiki-local
options.body: Avoid the public SDK addition and redesign the plugin integration around existing supported seams if that can preserve synchronous assembly.

options.title: Pause API expansion
options.body: Defer the refactor until maintainers define the intended async memory lifecycle and plugin compatibility policy.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Confirm the hook as the supported API, require digest-only prompt loading and focused compatibility coverage before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR body describes a maintainer-requested architecture and the supplied commit history shows this contributor carrying the relevant cache and SDK design.
